verification_audit.method: Duplicate-checked against the canonical repository before addition, then compared against the Madreag research corpus and independent Xenoverse 2 reference pages. Core acquisition and identity facts are promoted only where corroborated; unresolved technical or version-sensitive details remain partial.

records.name: Afterimage
records.character_source: Goku; Krillin; Tien; Yamcha; Piccolo; Gohan (Kid); Gohan (Teen); Gohan (Adult); Saibaman; Vegeta; Raditz; Burter; Appule; Captain Ginyu (Customize Partner); Jeice; Cell Jr.; Videl; Tapion
records.unlock_method: Skill Shop after the Raditz's Attack story saga; research corpus reports 1,000 Zeni and TP Medal rotation availability
records.source_quest_or_shop: Skill Shop / TP Medal Shop rotation
records.skill_description: A timed vanish that can evade incoming attacks and reposition the user behind a nearby opponent.
records.mechanics_notes: The research corpus describes Afterimage as a Ki-costing timed dodge rather than a stamina evasive. It can avoid incoming attacks when timed correctly and does not automatically damage or counterattack. Exact raw Ki data is represented as the canonical 100 Ki cost here, while frame timing remains version-sensitive.
records.combo_notes: The teleport reposition can create a back-facing punish opportunity, but the follow-up is manual rather than automatic.
records.pve_notes: Useful as an additional escape resource because it spends Ki instead of stamina, particularly when stamina is depleted or dangerous to spend.
records.pvp_notes: Timing is the central skill test: a successful cast can evade attacks and reposition, while a mistimed activation leaves the user vulnerable. Its different resource cost from a normal vanish is strategically important.

records.name: Aura Slide
records.unlock_method: TP Medal Shop limited-time rotation; research corpus reports 170 TP Medals while stocked
records.skill_description: A Ki-blade Strike Super with neutral, forward/up, and behind-the-user/down-input variants; variants can be chained and used while guarding.
records.mechanics_notes: Independent reference material corroborates the 100 Ki cost, Strike classification, short-range Ki-blade behavior, and directional variants. The research corpus additionally documents guard-casting, chaining up to four hits, and version-sensitive CaC damage testing; exact current damage should not be treated as universal.
records.combo_notes: The upward variant provides forward pressure and hitstun, while the downward variant can punish an opponent who vanishes behind the user. The multi-variant structure makes it useful inside strike strings.
records.pve_notes: Directional flexibility makes the skill useful for close-range AI pressure and for adapting the attack to the target's position.
records.pvp_notes: The rear-facing variant directly interacts with vanish behavior, while guard-casting and chained directional variants give it defensive and offensive utility. Exact damage has changed across versions.

records.name: Big Bang Knuckle
records.character_source: Vegeta (Super Saiyan God); Vegeta (Super Saiyan God) Ultra Supervillain; Vegeta (Customize Partner); Vegeta (Super Saiyan 4) (Customize Partner)
records.unlock_method: Parallel Quest 172 'Little Big Brother'; research corpus reports a 40% Ultimate Finish bonus-slot reward
records.skill_description: Fires a flurry of Ki Blasts and, if the attack connects, automatically chases the target and finishes with an aura-infused punch.
records.mechanics_notes: Independent reference material corroborates the PQ172 acquisition, 100 Ki cost, Strike classification, and approximately 11-hit structure. The research corpus describes up to seven ranged Ki Blasts followed by the chase punch and a known Final Rampage follow-up route.
records.combo_notes: The ranged opener can convert into the automatic chase and punch; the knockback ender can be routed into Final Rampage when the timing and target state allow.
records.pve_notes: The ranged opener gives the move useful reach against AI while the automatic chase supplies the close-range payoff.
records.pvp_notes: The opener extends the threat range of a Strike Super, but the projectile phase can still be defended against and a failed chase leaves the user exposed.

records.name: Burning Attack
records.unlock_method: Parallel Quest 41 'Warriors' Annihilation - Future Chapters'; research corpus reports a 30% Ultimate Finish reward and TP Medal rotation availability
records.skill_description: A hand-seal wind-up followed by a large Ki Blast that bursts on contact and launches the target vertically.
records.mechanics_notes: Independent reference material corroborates the 100 Ki cost, two-hit structure, and approximately 15% damage listing. The research corpus describes a roughly one-second startup, vertical launch, and brief trip state that can create a juggle opportunity.
records.combo_notes: Most reliable after a stun, knockdown, or spacing setup that covers the long hand-seal startup. The vertical launch can create follow-up opportunities.
records.pve_notes: The launch and trip behavior makes it useful for controlling a target's position and setting up subsequent attacks against AI.
records.pvp_notes: The reward for its launch utility comes with a readable startup; raw use against an attentive opponent is punishable, so it benefits from confirms and covered spacing.

records.name: Super Afterimage
records.character_source: Goku; Krillin; Tien; Yamcha; Piccolo; Raditz; Nappa; Vegeta; Zarbon; Dodoria; Captain Ginyu; Frieza (1st Form); Android 18; Cell (Perfect); Lord Slug; Majin Buu; Gohan (Adult); Gotenks; Turles; God of Destruction Beerus; Pan; Cooler (Final Form); Android 16; Gohan (Future); Bardock; Hit; Bojack
records.unlock_method: Skill Shop after completing 'The Ginyu Force Strikes' story saga; research corpus reports 4,500 Zeni and a TP Medal shop-tab listing
records.source_quest_or_shop: Skill Shop / TP Medal Shop tab
records.skill_description: Creates multiple afterimages that allow evasive movement and can reposition the user behind a nearby opponent.
records.mechanics_notes: The research corpus describes six afterimages, steerable movement during the effect, and a close-range reposition behind the opponent. The corpus also documents community zero-Ki defensive techniques. The exact interaction timing is technique- and version-sensitive.
records.combo_notes: It is primarily a movement/defensive tool rather than a damage skill. Skilled timing can turn the reposition into a back-facing offensive entry.
records.pve_notes: Useful for avoiding pressure and changing position without consuming Ki, especially for players who want a defensive movement option that does not spend stamina directly.
records.pvp_notes: Its value depends heavily on timing and movement control. Community techniques can extend its defensive utility, but the interaction should be documented as technique-dependent rather than guaranteed behavior.
